validity.recommendation: Add Budince Pipeline to OtherEnglishNames. Keep values. Length and diameter still need a citable source.
validity.researcher_notes: The line is real. Eustream says it was inaugurated and put into commercial operation on 2 September 2014 with 10 bcm per year, and Kyiv Post reported it in April 2014. It brings EU gas into Ukraine, so it is correctly a gas transmission interconnector. It is the same asset as the border point called Budince, not a duplicate of the Uzhhorod to Veľké Kapušany crossing (P3063), which is the older trunk crossing. The 700 mm diameter rests only on an ICIS article that cannot be cited. The earlier 8 to 9 bcm per year estimate was the same company's preliminary figure.

verifications.note: Eustream release dated 2 Sep 2014: Vojany-Uzhorod pipeline put into commercial operation
Kyiv Independent 9 Feb 2025: Ukraine imported gas that appeared to come from Hungary, Slovakia and Poland

fills.researcher_notes: The Eustream release of 2 September 2014 says the line went into commercial operation. A Kyiv Independent report of 9 February 2025 says Ukraine was still importing gas from Slovakia, but it does not name this pipeline. Eustream also still lists Budince as a working entry and exit point to Ukraine on its transmission page. Nothing found says the line is closed. The 2025 end of Russian transit does not touch this line, which only brings gas into Ukraine.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The newest dated evidence is a Kyiv Independent report of 9 February 2025 that Ukraine was importing gas that appeared to come from Hungary, Slovakia and Poland. It does not name this line. Eustream still lists Budince as an entry and exit point to Ukraine. This line carries gas into Ukraine, so the end of Russian transit on 1 January 2025 does not affect it. No source says it is closed. The evidence covers the Slovak to Ukraine crossing as a whole.
